_note: Dataset descriptors. Everything that depends on the input table (files, grid, provenance, column aliases, comparability, bundle format and folder, dataset-specific notes) lives here, never in the engine modules. Each setting has a value and a why, like engine_config.json. Every setting is also listed in /ASSUMPTIONS.md. Paths are relative to the 'tierra luna' directory.

default_dataset.why: The app ships the bundle built from the real 1-degree tables (open products, per-variable provenance). The legacy 2-degree table stays available for before-and-after comparison with --dataset legacy_2deg.

legacy_2deg.title: Legacy harmonized table, 2-degree grid
legacy_2deg.why: The team's committed table (output_py/earth_moon_harmonized_clean.csv). Almost every variable is a latitude formula or of undocumented origin (audit A2); kept only to compare before and after.

inputs.why: One CSV with both bodies (column 'body'), produced by main.py --pds per audit A2. The engine reads it and never regenerates it, because main.py rewrites tracked files.

input_csv.why: Same file as 'inputs' (kept under this name for the v1 code paths and tests that read it).

grid.why: 90 x 180 cells of 2 degrees, row 0 at the north, column 0 at the west; centre lat = 90 - (row + 0.5) * cell_deg, lon = -180 + (col + 0.5) * cell_deg; id = row * cols + col. The CSV column resolution_m = 500 is wrong (audit A2).

provenance.why: Levels, sources and comparability of the legacy table come from the audit-built registry (engine/build_provenance.py).

column_aliases.why: The legacy table already uses the mission variable names: every variable is read from the column of the same name.

column_overrides.why: No column substitution on the legacy table.

variables.why: Labels, units, kinds and descriptions come from the legacy registry (engine/provenance.json).

comparability.why: Comparability of the legacy variables is in the legacy registry (provenance.json comparable_across_bodies, built by engine/build_provenance.py COMPARABILITY).

bundle_format.why: Since engine 3.0.0 the legacy table is exported with the same v2 exporter as the real tables (three missions, funnel detail, similarity rules), so before-and-after comparisons and the tests use one contract. The v1 JSON exporter (engine/export.py) assumed a lunar twin for every ranked cell, which the default repo_global_mean rule does not have; it is kept in the code only for the physical_pooled rule and is no longer the legacy format.

bundle_version.why: Version of the v2 file structure, written in every file.

output_dir.why: The legacy build is for comparison only and is not shipped: it goes to a folder outside app/public. Pass --out to write it elsewhere.

earth_land_cells.why: Earth land cells of the legacy table are the cells passing the team's common land gate (elevation_m >= 1, written for the -250 m ocean fill).

value.cells: Earth cells that fail the common elevation_m land gate of mission_scoring.json (land = 0)

earth_ocean_fill.why: Audit A2 section 2a: the 10,273 ocean cells of earth_global_real.npz carry constant fills (-250 m, -1000 m, 0.01 deg, 0.1 m, 285 K, 0, -24 dB), and slope_300m_deg / rough_300m_m copy them. A fill is not a value, so the bundle writes null there and records the fill constants in earth_cells.json 'ocean_fill'. The engine itself still evaluates the team's land gate on the fill, as its why intends ('descarta oceano, que el modelo fija en -250 m'). Formula columns computed on the ocean (irradiance, rain, wind, mask_fraction, classes) are MODELLED values, not fills, and are kept.

region_max_place_km.why: A first-level region is exported only when the nearest GeoNames place is at most one Earth cell (222.4 km north-south for 2 degrees) from the cell centre and lies in the same country as the cell; farther away the region names another part of the country (review: Tibetan cells labelled 'Hebei', Franz Josef Land labelled 'Nenetskiy'). Otherwise region is null.

export_columns.why: The v1 bundle writes every registry variable as JSON.

lunar_named_sites.why: No named-site table was built for the legacy grid.

value: Lunar feature names: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, International Astronomical Union (IAU) Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature, and USGS Astrogeology Science Center (planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov).

Earth place names: GeoNames (geonames.org, CC BY 4.0) cities1000 list as packaged by the reverse_geocoder Python library (offline). Labels are the nearest populated place to the cell centre, not a boundary test.
Country names: ISO 3166 table iso3166.tab of the IANA time zone database (public domain), as shipped by the tzdata Python package.
Lunar elevation: LRO LOLA LDEM_4 (LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0), 8x8 block mean, NASA PDS Geosciences Node.
credits.why: Credits exported in manifest.json for the app's about box.

rover: Provisional team block. Interior Greenland ice-sheet cells rank near the top: the soft criteria have no surface-type term, ice counts as bare ground in rock_or_bare_frac, and 2-degree slope and roughness are smooth on an ice sheet. Whether ice or snow cells (thermal_inertia_class 'hielo') should be gated out is a question for Robotics 1; the engine does not change the gates.
solar: Rover and solar similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning; missions.json similarity); lunar_base keeps the repository's own z-score similarity (analog_finder) against the most similar cell of its lunar zone.
lunar_base: lunar_base is an exact copy of the thermal block; the ice block is shown per Earth cell as information only.
Lunar diurnal amplitude is a latitude-only formula (MODELLED) that Diviner contradicts at low and mid latitudes (R2 section 3, R3 F10 and F12).

mission_notes.why: Known limitations of each offered mission's results on the legacy table, exported in missions.json 'known_limitations'.

similarity_columns.why: The legacy table has every analog_finder variable under its own name; the repository similarity reads them as they are.

similarity_excluded.why: No exclusion on the legacy table: the repository formula is reproduced exactly (the test compares it with analog_finder.compute_analog_ranking on this table).

lunar_info_columns.why: No extra lunar information column on the legacy table.

supplements.why: No supplementary columns on this dataset (the supplementary tables are on the real 1-degree grid).

real_1deg.title: Real open-data tables, 1-degree grid
real_1deg.why: Earth from ETOPO 2022, ESA CCI land cover, the MODIS land surface temperature climatology, WorldClim 2.1 and the Obu permafrost maps; Moon from LOLA LDEM_16, Diviner and LOLA polar illumination (real_data/README.md). Every column has a provenance row with its level.

inputs.why: The two per-body tables written by real_data/build_earth.py and real_data/build_moon.py (earth_moon_real_1deg.csv is their concatenation). They are read at build time, never copied into code; an independent verifier may still correct them, so the bundle must be rebuilt after any change.

input_csv.why: Not used: this dataset has one input per body ('inputs').

grid.why: 180 x 360 cells of 1 degree per body, row 0 at the north (centre 89.5), column 0 at the west (centre -179.5), longitudes -180..180 east-positive; id = row * 360 + col. True cell size: 111.2 km north-south on Earth (6371 km sphere) and 30.3 km on the Moon; east-west it shrinks with cos(latitude). Earth latitudes are the products' WGS84 geodetic latitudes (at most 0.19 deg from geocentric, provenance_earth.csv).

provenance.why: Levels (MEASURED, DERIVED, MODELLED or no data), products, versions, licences, native resolutions, aggregation and caveats come from the builders' provenance files, read at build time. A level is never inferred from a column name; the row used is that of the real column a mission variable is read from.

column_aliases.why: Mission variable name (mission_scoring.json) to real column, with the true baseline and a caveat per body, written by the table builders.

column_overrides.why: Every slope variable the missions name (rover slope_300m_deg and solar slope_deg, both aliased to slope_deg) is read from the isotropic-baseline column instead, on both bodies. The literal slope_deg uses a one-pixel east-west spacing that shrinks as cos(latitude), so near the poles the east-west baseline falls to tens of metres and inflates the slope; both builders documented this (provenance rows of slope_deg, slope_p90_deg and slope_iso_deg). slope_iso_deg keeps the same baseline in both directions at every latitude (true baseline read from the provenance row). Equal to slope_deg at low latitudes.

elevation_m.label: Elevation
elevation_m.description: Mean surface height of the cell. Earth: land only, above the EGM2008 geoid (sea level). Moon: above the 1737.4 km reference sphere.

mask_fraction.label: Land share
mask_fraction.description: Earth: share of the cell that is land (ESA CCI land cover; inland water counts as water). Moon: 1 by definition.

slope_300m_deg.label: Slope (rover)
slope_300m_deg.description: The rover's slope variable. No global product has a 300 m baseline: it is read from the isotropic km-baseline slope (see true_baseline).

rough_300m_m.label: Roughness (rover)
rough_300m_m.description: The rover's roughness variable. RMS height difference (deviogram) at a lag of about 1.9 km, not 300 m (see true_baseline).

slope_deg.label: Slope
slope_deg.description: Mean slope of the cell at a km baseline (isotropic column, see true_baseline).

roughness_m.label: Roughness
roughness_m.description: RMS height difference (deviogram) at a lag of one DEM pixel, about 1.9 km.

rock_or_bare_frac.label: Bare or sparsely vegetated fraction
rock_or_bare_frac.description: Earth: bare plus sparse-vegetation share of the land pixels (ESA CCI land cover). Moon: 1 by definition (no vegetation); not rock abundance.

temp_k.label: Mean surface temperature
temp_k.description: Earth: annual mean clear-sky land surface temperature (mean of the ~10:30 and ~22:30 MODIS overpasses). Moon: diurnal mean Diviner bolometric brightness temperature.

lst_diurnal_amp_k.label: Diurnal surface temperature amplitude
lst_diurnal_amp_k.description: Earth: ~10:30 minus ~22:30 clear-sky land surface temperature (understates the daily range). Moon: maximum minus minimum of the Diviner diurnal curve.

tmin_c.label: Minimum temperature
tmin_c.description: Earth: coldest-month mean daily minimum AIR temperature (WorldClim 2.1, interpolated). Moon: minimum SURFACE brightness temperature (Diviner).

irradiance_kwh_m2_day.label: Solar irradiance
irradiance_kwh_m2_day.description: Daily solar energy on a horizontal surface. Earth: surface value under the atmosphere (WorldClim srad). Moon: geometry with no atmosphere, with the LOLA topographic lit fraction near the poles.

sun_elev_max_deg.label: Maximum sun elevation
sun_elev_max_deg.description: Highest sun elevation over the year at the cell-centre latitude (formula, flat horizon).

sun_low_frac_0_5deg.label: Low-sun fraction
sun_low_frac_0_5deg.description: Share of daylight time with the sun 0-5 degrees above a flat horizon (formula).

thermal_inertia_class.label: Thermal inertia class
thermal_inertia_class.description: Earth: ASSUMED mapping from ESA CCI land-cover classes (class_mappings.json). Moon: 'regolito' everywhere by assumption.

permafrost_class.label: Permafrost class
permafrost_class.description: Earth: class from the Obu et al. modelled permafrost probability. Moon: the label 'ninguno' (none) on every cell, a MODELLED label set by definition (team lead decision 5), not a measurement.

rain_mm_day.label: Precipitation
rain_mm_day.description: Earth: WorldClim 2.1 annual precipitation / 365.25. Moon: not applicable. Not used by the engine (only by rover workable_days, which mission_scoring.py does not read).

wind_max_ms.label: Windiest-month mean wind
wind_max_ms.description: Earth: WorldClim 2.1 windiest-month mean 10 m wind. Moon: not applicable. Not used by the engine (only by rover workable_days).

clear_frac_isccp.label: Clear-sky fraction (ISCCP satellite clouds)
clear_frac_isccp.description: Earth: 1 minus the mean ISCCP-H cloud amount over 2012-2016 (60 monthly means, NOAA NCEI ISCCP-H HGM v01r00, DERIVED). Moon: no data (no atmosphere). Licence: no constraints on data access or use; cite Rossow and Schiffer 1999.

variables.why: Display label, unit, kind and a short definition of each mission variable on this dataset. Definitions summarise real_data/provenance_*.csv and column_aliases.json; levels, sources and caveats are read from those files, not from here.

elevation_m.reason: Earth heights are above the geoid (sea level) and only over land; lunar heights are above an arbitrary 1737.4 km sphere. Not weighted by any mission (only the Earth land gate uses it).

mask_fraction.reason: Earth land share against a lunar value that is 1 by definition. Gate only.

slope_300m_deg.reason: Same definition on both bodies (central differences, isotropic baseline, cos-lat weighted cell mean) and near-equal baselines (3.7 km on Earth, 3.8 km on the Moon; true_baseline per body). Both are km-baseline slopes, not 300 m slopes.

rough_300m_m.reason: Same deviogram definition on both bodies at near-equal lags (1.853 km on Earth, 1.895 km on the Moon). Both are km-lag roughness, not 300 m roughness.

slope_deg.reason: Same definition and near-equal isotropic baselines on both bodies (see slope_300m_deg).

roughness_m.reason: Same deviogram definition at near-equal lags on both bodies (see rough_300m_m).

rock_or_bare_frac.reason: Earth bare-or-sparse-vegetation share from a land-cover classification against a lunar value that is 1 by definition; Moon-likeness would only measure how bare an Earth cell is.

temp_k.reason: Both are surface (skin) temperatures averaged over the day, but Earth is the mean of two clear-sky overpasses (~10:30 and ~22:30) and the Moon a full diurnal mean of a brightness temperature; Earth has no Antarctic values.

lst_diurnal_amp_k.reason: Both describe the daily swing of the surface temperature, but Earth is the difference between two satellite overpasses (~10:30 minus ~22:30), which understates the true daily range, while the lunar one is maximum minus minimum of the diurnal curve.

tmin_c.reason: Earth is an interpolated AIR temperature (coldest-month mean daily minimum, 2 m, WorldClim) while the lunar one is a SURFACE brightness temperature minimum; there is no air on the Moon. Different physical quantities.

irradiance_kwh_m2_day.reason: Daily energy on a horizontal surface on both bodies, but the Earth value is a MODELLED climatology of the solar radiation reaching the ground under the atmosphere and clouds (WorldClim interpolation, not a measurement) while the Moon has no atmosphere, and the lunar value is a 24-hour mean over a 29.5-day lunar day.

sun_elev_max_deg.reason: Same formula on both bodies (90 - max(0, |lat| - obliquity), flat horizon), each with its own obliquity.

sun_low_frac_0_5deg.reason: Same formula on both bodies (share of daylight with the sun 0-5 degrees high, flat horizon), each with its own obliquity.

thermal_inertia_class.reason: Earth classes are an assumed mapping from land cover; the lunar value is 'regolito' everywhere by assumption. A label match would say nothing physical.

permafrost_class.reason: Earth classes come from the Obu et al. modelled permafrost probability; the lunar value is the label 'ninguno' on every cell, a MODELLED label set by definition (team lead decision 5), not a measurement. A label match would say nothing physical.

clear_frac_isccp.reason: An Earth-only atmospheric quantity: the Moon has no clouds, so it enters the Solar panels suitability on Earth only, never the similarity.

comparability.why: One row per variable: whether the Earth and lunar values are the same physical quantity, decided from the definitions in the provenance files (pending team confirmation). 'not_comparable' variables are left out of the Earth-Moon similarity and the twin search but stay in suitability; 'comparable_with_caveat' variables are used and carry the reason to the interface.

bundle_format.why: Compact v2 bundle: JSON metadata plus little-endian binary typed arrays split into a small first view and on-demand files (docs/DATA_CONTRACT.md). The 1-degree tables are four times the legacy size, too big as JSON for a phone.

bundle_version.why: Version of the v2 file structure; also the folder name app/public/data/v2.

output_dir.why: Static folder served by the browser app with no server (relative to the 'tierra luna' directory).

earth_land_cells.why: The v2 bundle stores Earth cells that have any land (mask_fraction > 0: 25,497 of 64,800 when built), so the app can show why a coastal or lake cell fails (for example mask_fraction below the 0.3 gate, or elevation_m with no data). Pure-ocean cells (no land pixel) are left out of every Earth file; they fail every mission on the land gates.

earth_ocean_fill.why: The real tables have no ocean fills: a value without land is empty, and empty stays null.

region_max_place_km.why: A first-level region is shown only when the nearest GeoNames place is within one Earth cell (111.2 km north-south for 1 degree on the 6371 km sphere) and in the same country; same rule as the legacy 222.4 km for 2-degree cells.

export_columns.value: variables used by any mission gate, require_present or soft criterion
export_columns.why: Per-cell value columns written to the binary base files. rain_mm_day and wind_max_ms are only named by rover workable_days, which mission_scoring.py does not read, so they are described in variables.json but not stored (saves 0.2 MB). A column that is empty on a body (permafrost_class on the Moon) is not stored either; variables.json says so.

lunar_named_sites.why: IAU features that matter to the missions, with the 1-degree cell each falls in (written by real_data/build_moon.py). Exported with each site's per-mission pass flag and twin count; cell values are read from moon_base.bin, not copied.

value: Lunar feature names: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, International Astronomical Union (IAU) Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature, and USGS Astrogeology Science Center (planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov).

Earth place names: GeoNames (geonames.org, CC BY 4.0) cities1000 list as packaged by the reverse_geocoder Python library (offline). Labels are the nearest populated place to the cell centre, not a boundary test.
Country names: ISO 3166 table iso3166.tab of the IANA time zone database (public domain), as shipped by the tzdata Python package; country borders: Natural Earth 1:110m admin-0 (public domain).
credits.why: Credits for place names, exported in manifest.json. Data credits and licences are added at build time from the 'licence_credit' column of the provenance files, one entry per distinct product actually used.

rover: The rover thresholds (slope 0.5-15 deg, roughness 5-650 m) were written for a 300 m baseline and are applied unchanged to km-baseline values (slope over about 3.7-3.8 km, roughness at a lag of about 1.9 km). km-baseline slopes are much gentler than rover-scale slopes and km-lag roughness is larger than 300 m roughness, so passing these gates says nothing about rover-scale hazards. Nothing was adjusted (known limitation, pending Robotics 1).

Similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances, on slope and roughness only, 50 % each (decision of 2026-11-15 11:23 CET): the twin is the cell of the lunar south-polar zone (75-90 S) whose slope is within 2 deg and roughness within 30 m of the Earth cell (illustrative values of the team's rover file for a 5 km baseline), with the highest similarity. Relative elevation is no longer compared (it has no physical sense for a rover); it is shown per pair as a difference. A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score.

Relative elevation, temperature, diurnal amplitude and irradiance are not part of the rover similarity: their values on both sides and the difference are shown for information (the lunar south-polar twins are colder than their Earth points by a median of about 150 K).
solar: The solar twin is matched on sunlight above the atmosphere (team decision of 2026-11-15, morning): Earth's annual-mean sunlight at the top of the atmosphere (DERIVED from latitude) against the lunar surface irradiance of the equatorial maria (|lat| <= 30 deg, elevation <= -1,200 m), within 0.6 kWh/m2/day, with slope and roughness as secondary criteria. Only part of that sunlight reaches the ground on Earth (shown per pair); on the Moon all of it does, in a lunar day of 29.5 Earth days. The maria receive the sunlight of Earth's tropics, so only points within about 33.5 deg of the equator find a twin; the others keep their suitability with no twin (missions.json similarity.unpaired_reasons).

Earth irradiance at the ground, sun geometry and the diurnal amplitude are suitability criteria. Earth irradiance at the ground is surface solar energy under the atmosphere and clouds (WorldClim) and lunar irradiance is airless geometry; the solar gates on irradiance, maximum sun elevation and low-sun fraction would remove the lunar cells nearer the poles (shown only when a lunar cell is inspected: lunar cells are not filtered for the similarity).

Temperature and diurnal amplitude are not part of the solar similarity: their values on both sides and the difference are shown for information. 6,060 passing solar cells (all in Antarctica) have no land surface temperature: the amplitude weight drops out of their suitability with the remaining weights renormalised. None of them has a lunar twin (they lie at 64.5 S or further south, far from the latitudes whose sunlight matches the maria), so they have no similarity, no final score and no confidence.
lunar_base: The Lunar base criteria are an exact copy of the team's thermal block (team design values, no external source). The ice block is shown per Earth cell as information only (passes or not, its suitability) and never changes this ranking; no lunar cell passes ice because the lunar permafrost class is the MODELLED label 'none', which the ice gate excludes.

Similarity is a likeness of thermal POSITION and real terrain, not of temperature (team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET): the coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as percentiles within each population (Earth: the points passing this mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole), each within 10 percentile points, and slope and roughness in real values (within 4 deg and 60 m). Equal positions do not mean equal temperatures: on every pair the twin is far colder and swings far more than the Earth point, and the real values and differences are shown with every pair. A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score.

The coldest temperature is a MODELLED air temperature on Earth (WorldClim, coldest month, interpolated) and a MEASURED surface temperature on the Moon (Diviner night minimum); the Earth diurnal amplitude is a difference between two satellite overpasses and understates the daily range. Both are suitability criteria on Earth, and in the similarity only their position within each population is compared, never their values.
Antarctica has no land surface temperature product here, so its cells fail for lack of a daily temperature swing value ('no data').

mission_notes.why: Known limitations of each offered mission's results on the real tables, exported in missions.json 'known_limitations' next to computed 'facts'. Written after seeing the results; nothing was tuned. 2026-11-15 11:23 CET: the Rover notes describe the slope-and-roughness similarity; the Rover ice note with typed figures is replaced by the computed text similarity.json texts.surface_classes_rover (engine_config limit_texts), which is also on the mission card.

elevation_rel_m.note: The real tables have no elevation_rel_m. The repository defines it as elevation_m minus the body's mean (earth_extractor.py, lunar_extractor.py; on the legacy table the difference is the constant -1047.422 m on every Earth land cell). A per-body z-score is unchanged by subtracting a constant (median and spread shift with it), so z is computed from elevation_m; the absolute value exported is elevation_m (Earth above the geoid, Moon above the 1737.4 km sphere).

slope_deg.note: The mission-view slope_deg, i.e. the isotropic-baseline column slope_iso_deg on both bodies (column_overrides).

roughness_m.note: Deviogram roughness at a ~1.9 km lag on both bodies.

temp_k.note: Earth: mean of two clear-sky MODIS overpasses (empty in Antarctica); Moon: Diviner diurnal mean.

rock_or_bare_frac.note: 1 on every lunar cell by definition; removed from the similarity (similarity_excluded).

sar_sigma0_db.note: No radar column in the real tables: the variable has no data on either body and the repository rule (valid on both bodies) drops it; its weight is renormalised away.

similarity_columns.why: Real column read for each analog_finder similarity variable on each body (team lead decision 3). The repository's six variables keep their names; only elevation_rel_m is read from elevation_m (note) and sar_sigma0_db has no column.

value.rock_or_bare_frac: Team lead decision 3: rock_or_bare_frac is 1 on every lunar cell by definition (provenance_moon.csv: MODELLED), so it has no variation on the Moon; the repository's normaliser would give every lunar cell z = 0 and still count the variable. It is removed from the similarity on the real tables and its weight is redistributed among the remaining variables in proportion to their weights; it is shown as information only. Diviner rock abundance (rock_abundance_frac) is a different quantity and is not substituted.

similarity_excluded.why: Variables removed from the repository similarity on this dataset, each with the team lead's reason. The remaining DEFAULT_WEIGHTS are divided by their sum (proportional redistribution).

rock_abundance_frac.label: Diviner rock abundance
rock_abundance_frac.note: Areal fraction of the surface covered by rocks larger than about 1 m (Diviner, 60S-60N only; empty poleward). A different quantity from rock_or_bare_frac: information only, never used by a mission or the similarity.

lunar_info_columns.why: Lunar columns exported as information next to the lunar values (team lead decision 3 allows the Diviner rock abundance as a separate lunar information value with its source). Level and source come from provenance_moon.csv.

value.caveat: ISCCP-H HGM v01r00 (NOAA NCEI) mean clear-sky fraction 2012-2016, 1 - cloud amount; DERIVED; least reliable over snow, ice and polar night; cloud amount is not irradiance

supplements.why: Supplementary columns joined by cell id at load time (engine.dataset.load_supplements), each with its own provenance file, so a new measured column does not require rebuilding the big tables. clear_frac_isccp: research 2 option E2, approved by the team lead at 11:51 CET on 2026-11-15 (docs/stats_audit/research_2_solar_idoneidad.md); written by tierra luna/research/r2_build_cloud.py from ISCCP-H HGM v01r00 (NOAA NCEI, 2012-2016); cite Rossow and Schiffer 1999, BAMS 80:2261-2287.
